title: Copilot Studio: computer use for web browsing on the Microsoft Copilot harness
summary: Hold: the credit-allocation API instruction omits the environment scope and allocation body needed to perform the operation. The page also incorrectly treats the applicability of environment cost controls as unconfirmed, although Microsoft explicitly documents their platform-wide scope. The roadmap dates and distinction between planned browsing and existing standard-harness computer use are supported.

claims.claim: The FAQ advises trusted, isolated environments to reduce these risks.
claims.quote: To reduce these risks, operate computer use in trusted, isolated environments and apply robust validation checks before executing any instructions.

claims.claim: The applicability of the existing tool's prompt-injection guidance to this planned browsing implementation is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Copilot harness" "computer use" "human supervision" "identity" "audit"; opened computer use FAQ, harness overview and computer use. Guidance concerns the existing tool; the harness comparison still says Planned.

claims.quote: If you share an agent with this setting, anyone using it can act with the original author's access on the configured machine.

claims.claim: Tenant-pool draw is configured at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select **Licensing**. ... Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**. ... Select **Manage Copilot Credits**. ... Select the environment. ... Under **Capacity overages**, clear **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**.

claims.claim: The printed PUT instruction with entitlementId MCSMessages and a TenantPool enforcementRules entry is a complete operation to allocate environment credits and disable tenant-pool draw.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } ... allocatedEntitlements = @( ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } ... enforcementRules = @( ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api.call and the rendered call with: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 with Authorization: Bearer <access-token>, Content-Type: application/json, and body {"scope":{"environmentId":"<environment-id>"},"allocatedEntitlements":[{"entitlementId":"MCSMessages","allocation":{"quantity":<credits>},"enforcementRules":[{"ruleType":"TenantPool","enabled":false}]}]}. The cited tutorial supplies the method, base URL, version and body; its use of variables explains the pre-check's literal-URL miss, but the omitted scope and allocation remain a real defect.

claims.claim: A linked pay-as-you-go plan can permit continued usage after the environment exhausts its prepaid allocation.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph beginning Both rows
claims.claim: Neither table row is confirmed by Microsoft to govern browsing on the Microsoft Copilot harness, including the environment cost-control row.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.fix: Replace the paragraph with: 'Both rows are controls that exist today. Microsoft has not confirmed that the first, documented for the standard harness, governs browsing on the Microsoft Copilot harness. The second governs prepaid capacity for the whole environment across Copilot Studio, including Microsoft Copilot harness agents; a linked pay-as-you-go plan can still allow usage.' In the summary and risk rationale, narrow 'controls for this harness are not yet documented' to 'browsing-specific access and identity controls are not yet documented', so the gap does not obscure documented platform-wide cost controls.

claims.claim: The environment allocation is shared across other Copilot Studio agents and features, rather than being exclusive to browsing.
claims.quote: Changes to shared capacity can affect other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in the same environment.

claims.claim: The standard-harness Hosted browser in computer use tenant setting is under Power Platform admin center > Manage > Tenant settings.
claims.quote: To disable the hosted browser in a tenant: ... On the side bar select **Manage** and then select **Tenant settings**. ... Select **Hosted browser in computer use**.

claims.claim: The standard-harness computer use tool includes an Enforce HTTPS option.
claims.quote: Turn on **Enforce HTTPS** to ensure computer use works only with HTTPS websites

claims.claim: Agent monthly limits are set through Manage Agents in the Copilot Studio licensing area.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, go to **Licensing** > **Copilot Studio**. ... Select **Manage Agents**. ... Select the agent, and then select **Set limit**.

claims.claim: A published environment group rule governing tenant-pool draw makes the environment-level setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override a published environment group rule governing tenant-pool draw.
claims.quote: The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: A page-visit audit trail for this planned Microsoft Copilot harness browsing capability is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Copilot harness" "computer use" "human supervision" "identity" "audit". Opened harness overview and read Monitor computer use excerpts. The documented screenshots, website activity and CUAOperation logging concern the standard-harness tool.

claims.claim: All controls that the governance checklist tells readers to configure or inspect are represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Limit who can author ... using environment permissions'; 'set an agent monthly limit with Stop usage'; 'Use the Harness column'. Table: Computer use environment setting and environment credit allocation only.
claims.fix: The checklist steps for authoring permissions, agent monthly limits and Harness-column inventory inspection have no corresponding controls-table rows. This finding identifies the mismatch only; it does not request additional rows or unverified control details.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Cost and licensing: Caps
claims.claim: An agent monthly limit with Stop usage provides a workload stopping point.
claims.quote: To create a workload-level stopping point, also configure an agent limit with **Stop usage**.
claims.fix: Qualify the 'hard stop' guidance with: 'Limits are not applied instantly, so allow a margin in limits and notification thresholds. An agent monthly limit does not stop agent flows it calls; those are checked separately against environment capacity.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity#manage-monthly-consumption-limits-for-copilot-studio-agents, which explicitly gives both qualifications.
